summary: Added Playwright 1.63.0 (+ @axe-core/playwright 4.13.0), playwright.config.ts (webServer `npm run start` on 4200, reuseExistingServer, chromium only, retain-on-failure traces) and 6 spec files under e2e/ covering the app's five primary journeys: browse the tutorials list, search by title, add a tutorial, publish/unpublish/delete via the details drawer, and edit a tutorial at /tutorials/:id — each with populated, empty, error and not-found states. The backend (http://localhost:5001/api) is not running in CI, so every spec stubs it with page.route using the contract shapes from TutorialService/Tutorial, and the specs assert on the requests the UI actually sent (method, url, payload) as well as on rendered output. Last local run: 29 passed, 0 failed, 7 skipped (stable across 3 runs). PARTIAL because three real application defects are left as failing/`fixme` tests rather than papered over: the /api/health + footer "API: ok" story is not implemented at all, the Add Tutorial form performs no validation, and every page has serious axe violations. Line coverage is not measured for e2e; the flows above exercise all 4 routes and all 5 components.

test_files.description: Tutorials list: populated/empty/API-error states, search by title (match and no match), Remove All success and failure.

Add Tutorial: successful POST with the typed payload, Add another resets the form, API rejection shows no success, and the missing-validation defect (one fixme + one test documenting current behaviour).
Details drawer: opens with the clicked tutorial, 404 shows Not found, publish/unpublish send the right PUT, delete closes and refreshes, failed delete keeps the drawer, close button, Edit navigation.

Edit page at /tutorials/:id: loads by route id, Update sends edited fields and confirms, failed update shows no confirmation, UnPublish flips the pill, Delete returns to the list, unknown id shows the fallback.
The GET /api/health + footer "API: ok" story: two fixme tests for the intended behaviour plus one passing test documenting that the footer renders no API status.
Axe smoke per key page and for the open drawer: serious+critical checks kept as fixme KNOWN-DEFECT, critical-only checks run as regression guards.
Shared page.route backend stub (list/detail/404/write-error variants) returning contract response shapes and recording the calls the app made.

findings.title: GET /api/health and the footer "API: ok" indicator are not implemented
findings.description: The requested story is absent from the app: nothing requests /api/health, and src/app/app.component.html renders only "© Tutorial Manager" and "Built with Angular" in the footer. There is no health check, no status text and no failure state.
findings.test: e2e/health-footer.spec.ts :: shows "API: ok" in the footer when the health endpoint reports ok
findings.evidence: With GET **/api/health stubbed to 200 {"status":"ok"}, expect(page.getByRole('contentinfo')).toContainText('API: ok') fails — the footer text is "© Tutorial Manager Built with Angular". No /api/health request appears in the network log. Reproduced 3/3 runs and confirmed in the live browser at http://localhost:4200/tutorials.

findings.title: Add Tutorial submits an empty form with no validation and reports success
findings.description: The title and description inputs carry `required`, but the component is not inside a <form> with Angular validation and saveTutorial() never checks the values. Clicking Submit on an untouched form POSTs {"title":"","description":""} and, on a 200, shows "Tutorial was submitted successfully!" — so a user can create blank tutorials whenever the API accepts them.
findings.test: e2e/add-tutorial.spec.ts :: does not submit an empty form and reports a validation error (fixme)
findings.evidence: Empty submit records a POST with body {"title":"","description":""} in the page.route call log and the success alert becomes visible; the intended-behaviour test asserting zero POSTs fails 3/3 runs. Current behaviour is pinned by the passing test "empty submit currently POSTs an empty tutorial and shows success".

findings.title: Serious accessibility violations on every page (colour contrast, <li> outside a list)
findings.description: Axe reports `serious` violations on all key pages: insufficient colour contrast on .app-footer-note, .tm-subtitle and .badge-primary, and `listitem` because the header nav renders <li> elements directly inside <div class="navbar-nav"> with no <ul>/<ol> parent. Per the org standard, serious/critical violations are findings.
findings.test: e2e/accessibility.spec.ts :: the tutorials list page has no serious or critical accessibility violations (fixme)
findings.evidence: AxeBuilder().analyze() on /tutorials, /add, /tutorials/1 and the open drawer: "serious: color-contrast [.tm-subtitle | .badge-primary | .app-footer-note]" and "serious: listitem — <li> elements must be contained in a <ul> or <ol> [li:nth-child(1) | li:nth-child(2)]". Reproduced 3/3 runs. Also non-blocking: moderate page-has-heading-one, minor aria-allowed-role.

findings.title: Failed API requests are only logged to the console — the UI shows no error state
findings.description: Every subscriber in TutorialsListComponent, AddTutorialComponent and TutorialDetailsComponent handles errors with console.error only. A failed GET /tutorials leaves `tutorials` undefined, so the user sees the "No tutorials yet" empty state instead of an error; a failed Remove All, Update or Delete silently does nothing.
findings.test: e2e/tutorials-list.spec.ts :: shows the empty state when the tutorials request fails
findings.evidence: With GET /api/tutorials stubbed to 500 the page renders the "No tutorials yet" heading and no alert; the browser console shows the HttpErrorResponse. The test asserts this current behaviour rather than the desired error banner, so the gap is documented instead of hidden.
